newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: TABLE-Malaysia stocks seen weaker - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: TABLE-Malaysia stocks seen weaker - Reuters poll.

text.p: Malaysian stocks are expected to head lower on a technical basis in the near-term, analysts said in a Reuters poll on Wednesday.
A Reuters poll of 10 brokerages and fund managers showed that the blue-chip Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index could dip to an average 907.2, with a firmer support level at 858.3.
The new resistance level for the key index was seen at an average level of 1,000.8.
Forecasts for the immediate support level ranged from the low 800s to 950 points.
On Tuesday, the index closed at 945.08. The index fell to a new 1997 low of 936.12 on Wednesday.

The index has fallen around six percent over the last three days as Malaysia announced a 2.8 billion ringgit trade deficit for June and restricted currency swap transactions by local banks in order to reduce speculation in the ringgit.

Malaysian stock prices have been in the doldrums since late March, when the central Bank Negara announced curbs on banks' lending to the property sector and for share purchases. The blue-chip index has lost 22 percent since March 28 and over 25 percent since its peak of 1,278.94 on February 26.
